dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: protagonist

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Are there others like me? How many women have you stolen and brought here?

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The last restraint falls away. I rub my wrists — raw from struggling. The creatures in the shadows lean closer. Their eyes reflect the firelight like dozens of dying stars.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Angel stands over me. His coat falls open. Beneath it, his body is pale and carved from marble — scarred in places, ancient in places. He is beautiful in the way a cathedral is beautiful: vast, cold, and built for worship.

dialogue.speaker: angel
dialogue.text: You wanted to know about the others. There were many. None lasted. None pleased me the way you already have.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: He climbs onto the bed. The mattress dips under his weight. His cold hands part my knees. I should run. The door is somewhere behind the creatures. I could try.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: What do you want from me?

dialogue.speaker: angel
dialogue.text: Everything. Your fear. Your pleasure. Your surrender. I want to hear you scream my name while they watch. I want you to forget you ever lived anywhere but here.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: His mouth finds my neck — the same spot where his fangs pierced me. He doesn't bite. He kisses the wound. A apology or a claim. I can't tell the difference anymore.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: His hands explore me like I'm a map of something he's been looking for. Every touch is deliberate. Every caress is a question. And my body answers without my permission — arching, trembling, begging.

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.text: Who were they? How many women has he brought here before me?

The second holds a stone basin filled with dark liquid that reflects no light. The third holds nothing — just an empty pedestal with scratches in the stone where something was taken.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Days pass. Or what feels like days. Time moves differently here. The fire never goes out. The torches never dim. Angel comes and goes — sometimes staying for hours, sometimes vanishing for what feels like weeks.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: He brings me clothes — real clothes, not just torn lingerie. Black silks and deep purples, fabrics so soft they feel like smoke against my skin. He brings food I don't need but crave. Wine that tastes like dark berries and old secrets.

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.speaker: protagonist

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: And if I wanted to leave?

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: protagonist

dialogue.speaker: protagonist

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: protagonist

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: That's what you tell yourself? That you're a savior?

dialogue.speaker: narrator

dialogue.speaker: angel
dialogue.text: Hunters. They found the breach. They've been looking for a way in for centuries.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: What do they want?

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The cracks widen. Figures begin to push through — men and women in dark tactical gear, carrying weapons I don't recognize. They move with military precision. They've done this before.

dialogue.speaker: angel

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: I raise my hands. The purple light explodes from my fingertips. The walls seal. The fire roars back to life. And the hunters scream as the Domain fights back — through me.
